small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_N×BLOCK_OC tiles like (128,128) and (256,128) with num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 — current best uses 128×64 which underutilizes registers; OC=64 means a single OC tile per program, freeing the OC grid dimension and letting BLOCK_N grow.
- Swap the program-id ordering / add an L2 swizzle (group_size on pid_n) so that consecutive programs along N reuse the same weight tile in L2; weights are tiny (64·72·4B≈18KB) but reordering still improves cache hit rate at the K-loop boundary.
- Hoist `HW`, `OW`, `OH*OW`, and the `(b, oh, ow)` decomposition once; precompute `x_n_base` and `nhw_offset` together — and try BLOCK_K=72 (=K_TOTAL exactly) with a single iteration of the K-loop, eliminating the outer `for` and its masking entirely.
large_guidance:
- Switch to a channels-last (NHWC) layout: permute input to (B,H,W,IC), pack weight as (KH,KW,IC,OC). The GEMM-K dimension (IC·KH·KW) then has IC as the innermost contiguous axis, giving fully coalesced 128-bit loads across BLOCK_K instead of the current strided gather over IC·H·W.
- Make the kernel persistent over output tiles per SM and fix BLOCK_OC=64 (==OC), so the entire OC dimension is one tile and the inner loop only iterates K_TOTAL=72 once; this eliminates the OC program grid and lets one program emit the full output channel vector per spatial tile, reducing weight reloads.
- Specialize for KH=KW=3 with a fully unrolled 9-tap loop (no K-loop, no k-mask): generate 9 explicit `tl.load` of input slices at compile-time offsets and 9 FMAs against constexpr-indexed weight slices, which removes BLOCK_K masking overhead and shrinks the inner loop to dense FMAs.
